tagline: The Great Skyroad, open when the snow allows.
intro: Out of Centennial, WYO 130 climbs west into the Medicine Bow Mountains, from 8,000 feet on the valley floor through spruce-fir forest, where the wind shapes the krummholz near the top, to 10,847 feet at Snowy Range Pass. Medicine Bow Peak stands over it, and even deep into summer last winter's snow still caps the high ground. Then the road comes down the west slope toward Saratoga.
It was a wagon trail in the 1870s. Highway work began in the 1920s and took six years, and the finished road was known as the Great Skyroad.
season: WYDOT's byway guide says the wildflower displays peak in late summer.

moments.title: Centennial
moments.text: Gold turned up on Centennial Ridge in 1875, the town took its name the next year for the nation's hundredth birthday, and most of the gold was gone by 1877.

moments.title: Libby Flats
moments.text: At the summit an observation point looks south as far as the Rawah and Never Summer wilderness areas in Colorado, and a short loop trail reaches the 1920s Red Mask Mine.

moments.title: Lake Marie
moments.text: Down from the summit, glacier-fed Mirror Lake and its sister Lake Marie both reflect Medicine Bow Peak, a ridge of quartzite reckoned at two billion years old.

practical: Snow closes the high section of the road every winter. Plows traditionally open it in May, before Memorial Day weekend.
